extracted.intended_audience: TeX/LaTeX users who need to typeset graphs and diagrams (mathematicians, category theorists, computer scientists, etc.)
extracted.subtask_short: typesetting graphs and diagrams with Xy-pic
extracted.subtask_description: Using the Xy-pic TeX package to create and typeset graphs, commutative diagrams, knots, polygons, and other diagrammatic material; covers modes, object types, arrow/path notation, backends (PS/PDF), documentation and support resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical composition of visual components
rubrics_metrics.description: Xy-pic is a package for typesetting graphs and diagrams using the principle of logical composition of visual components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Diagrams are constructed by composing visual components; the package is structured into modules (options) each defining mnemonic plain-text notation for particular graphical objects or structures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modular structure: kernel + options
rubrics_metrics.description: Xy-pic is structured as a kernel and several orthogonal modules called options, each defining a custom notation for a particular kind of graphical object or structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options are combinable and provide different composition structures (graph, matrix-like, polygon, knot, turtle graphics, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Graph combinator mode
rubrics_metrics.description: A graph combinator mode where diagrams are specified the way they are composed as graphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this mode when you want to define diagrams by nodes and edges (graph composition) rather than by matrix alignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix-like (diagram) mode
rubrics_metrics.description: A matrix-like mode where the dimensions of the drawing are computed by aligning diagram entries in rows and columns (the diagram mode Xy-pic version 2 users are used to).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for commutative diagrams and layouts where entries align in a grid; behaves like a matrix to compute spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polygon mode
rubrics_metrics.description: A polygon mode where diagrams shaped as regular polygons are entered in a simple way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenient for symmetric polygonal arrangements of nodes and edges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Knot and links mode
rubrics_metrics.description: A mode for typesetting beautiful knots and links.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides specialized primitives and layout for knot diagrams and related topological illustrations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Object-oriented turtle graphics mode
rubrics_metrics.description: A general object-oriented turtle graphic drawing language for specifying graphs with objects and connections between them in a manner independent of orientation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good for programmatic generation of diagrams where relative movements and object-oriented constructs are convenient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible position specifications
rubrics_metrics.description: Positions can be given in a variety of formats (extendable) including user defined coordinates (x,y) and relative to previous positions, objects, object edges, and points on connections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple coordinate systems supported; you can position elements absolutely or relatively to other objects/edges/points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for multiple object shapes and adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects may be circular, elliptic, or rectangular (more shapes can be added) and adjusted in several ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shapes are extensible; objects can be customized in size and appearance to fit diagram needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large library of mnemonic-named objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Large library of objects with mnemonic names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Predefined objects speed up diagram construction; users can rely on mnemonic names rather than low-level drawing commands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects that orient along connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects that orient themselves along a connection when placed relative to it, e.g., @{|-} is like \vdash but thus oriented; new such objects can be defined in a convenient way.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows symbols to rotate to follow edge directions; facilitates consistent arrowheads or markers aligned with paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of TeX boxes for text and math
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX boxes, i.e., text and mathematical formulae, can be used as objects within diagrams.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typeset labels and formulae as normal TeX content inside nodes/boxes for high-quality integration with surrounding text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for circle segments and arbitrary arcs
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes circle segments and optionally arbitrary elliptical, quadratic, and cubic arcs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enable curved edges and arc segments; some arc types may require backend support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Connections aligned between reference points and edge endpoints
rubrics_metrics.description: Connections are aligned between the reference points of objects but start and end on the edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Connections calculate alignment from object reference points but are drawn to meet object edges, giving neat joins between nodes and paths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any object usable to build connections (diagonal filling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any object can be used to build a connection (using diagonal filling); library objects provide common line types.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can create custom path styles by composing objects; built-in line types cover common needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible arrow and path notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Flexible notation for drawing arrows and general paths with tail, stem, and head built from any object(s). Special support for arrows that cross each other, arrows that go by other entries, paired arrows (including support for 2-cells), curved arrows, and arrows with bends. The style of arrow tips can be configured to match several styles of symbol arrows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extensive arrow styling allows representation of complex categorical/graphical relations, crossings, 2-cells, and custom tip shapes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Library of frames and braces
rubrics_metrics.description: Library of frames and braces.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use prebuilt frames and braces to group or annotate parts of diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotation, scaling, colour, and line thickness notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Special notation for rotation, scaling, colour, and line thickness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correct typesetting of these features requires a backend that supports it, but when not available Xy-pic tries to approximate what is requested so that at least the picture size is stable (and thus page breaks).

rubrics_metrics.name: PostScript output and literal inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Output can use PostScript for drawing (several \special formats are supported: dvips, Textures, and OzTeX). Notation for inclusion of literal PostScript is available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PostScript backends for precise drawn output; contact maintainers for currently supported drivers and formats.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF output support (xypdf)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support for Adobe PDF output is available from version 3.8. The xypdf package provides detailed user and TeXnical documentation of the PDF support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDF backend enables direct PDF output; see xypdf for instructions and font conversion notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compatibility with TeX formats and distributions
rubrics_metrics.description: Xy-pic works with most formats, including all variants of LaTeX, AMS-TeX, and plain TeX, and is often included with TeX installations (e.g., part of the pictures bundle in TeX Live).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be available in common TeX distributions; if not, obtain from CTAN or SourceForge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive documentation set
rubrics_metrics.description: Official documentation consists of: Xy-pic User's Guide, Xy-pic Reference Manual, Xy-pic Complete Sources with TeXnical Commentary, and the xypdf package documentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: User's Guide for basic matrix-like diagrams; Reference Manual for syntax and semantics; Complete Sources for in-depth TeXnical commentary; xypdf for PDF backend details. Documentation PDFs are updated with each release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tutorials, examples, and community resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Several tutorials and example collections exist (An Introduction to Xy-pic; Commutative Diagrams with XY-pic; LaTeX Graphics Companion chapter; examples and papers on CTAN; various tutorials and HTML/PDF guides).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use tutorials for learning patterns and see example archives for ready-made diagrams; contributions and pointers to other resources are encouraged via the mailing list.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help and support via mailing list (TUG)
rubrics_metrics.description: Help and support on Xy-pic matters, and announcements of new versions, are provided by the Xy-pic mailing list, graciously hosted by TUG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subscribe to the mailing list for support, announcements, and community discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distribution and licensing: free software availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Xy-pic is © by its authors as free software and is available from CTAN or the SourceForge development project home.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check CTAN/SourceForge for current releases; many TeX installations include Xy-pic by default.
